items.title: `exclude-newer`: Parsing failures should become an error
items.reason: Closest canonical discussion: uv sync continues after a settings-discovery parse warning and ignores exclude-newer. A maintainer confirmed this was unintended and noted that making it fatal is breaking. The new report adds unknown fields as another trigger for the same configuration-discarding behavior.

items.title: Fail on `exclude-newer` parse errors
items.reason: Existing draft targeting astral-sh/uv#18922, opened months before this report. Its description explicitly discusses reconsidering settings parse failures more broadly, but limits the proposal to exclude-newer. The author deferred merging it in July 2026; it is not a shipped fix.

items.title: tool.uv.required-version should be handled before parsing rest of pyproject.toml file
items.reason: Historical instance of the same parse failure discarding another setting: unsupported configuration bypassed required-version. This narrower version-enforcement bug was fixed; the new report does not establish a regression of that fix.

items.title: Elevate configuration errors to `required-version` mismatches
items.reason: Merged April 13, 2026, fixing astral-sh/uv#17609 by checking required-version after settings parsing fails. Current source retains this check but still warns and skips the file when no version mismatch is found; it does not implement general fatal validation.

items.title: `pyproject.toml` TOML parse error/warning shown twice
items.reason: Adjacent settings-discovery discussion whose comments propose making parse failures fatal. Its reproduction has invalid TOML syntax and already ends in an error; this report concerns schema-invalid settings that can allow execution to succeed.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs using authenticated gh. Literal searches covered settings discovery, unknown field, pyproject.toml parse warnings, exclude-newer, and required-version. Conceptual searches covered ignored configuration, invalid settings, fatal parsing, strict mode, warnings as errors, and CI configuration validation, without incidental package/version/platform restrictions. Fix-oriented searches and issue timelines led to astral-sh/uv#18923, astral-sh/uv#18977, and astral-sh/uv#6009; inspected their descriptions, comments, and reviews alongside current source and existing snapshots. PR keyword searches returned no hits, so linked PRs were inspected directly. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#5934 and its merged fix astral-sh/uv#6009 as diagnostic-detail improvements rather than fatal-validation fixes; astral-sh/uv#9653 requests a separate validation command; astral-sh/uv#3097 restricts executable lookup. Reporter links astral-sh/uv#6662 and astral-sh/uv#16546 concern uv bootstrapping and package-file conflicts respectively. Also inspected astral-sh/uv#22950 and astral-sh/uv#17308: preview semantics and workspace-dependent discovery are not the canonical discussion for this request.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#18922 already tracks the underlying correctness problem: settings parse failures become warnings, configuration is discarded, and execution continues. The unknown-field example and request for broader or opt-in fatal validation can be discussed there, with the existing draft astral-sh/uv#18923. Duplicate classification takes precedence. The merged astral-sh/uv#18977 only fixed required-version enforcement, so this is not evidence that a general parse-error fix regressed.
summary: astral-sh/uv#18922 and its open draft astral-sh/uv#18923 are the closest matches. astral-sh/uv#17609 and astral-sh/uv#18977 document the narrower, already-fixed required-version case; astral-sh/uv#9911 covers duplicate parse diagnostics.
draft_response: You're right that a settings parse failure can discard otherwise-valid settings from the same `pyproject.toml`. This is the underlying behavior tracked in astral-sh/uv#18922. The targeted proposal in astral-sh/uv#18923 is still an open draft, and making these failures fatal needs a compatibility decision. Please add your unknown-field example and request for broader validation to astral-sh/uv#18922 so we can keep the discussion together.
